meta.bannerMessage: Six of the eight projects have flown under the program as of October 22, 2026. Florida and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey have announced no eIPP flight. Participants bear their own costs.

summaryBlocks.heading: What Has Flown
summaryBlocks.body: Pennsylvania's team first, on July 10, 2026, then Utah, Louisiana, Texas, North Carolina and Albuquerque. Most flights used conventional-takeoff airplanes (BETA's ALIA CTOL, Cessna Caravans, Electra's EL2) or, in Texas, helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft. Louisiana's Elroy Air Chaparral flew with nobody on board. No flight has carried passengers.

summaryBlocks.heading: Cargo Signal
summaryBlocks.body: Louisiana, Albuquerque, North Carolina, Utah and Florida's first phase lead with cargo or medical logistics. The flights so far have carried an organ for United Therapeutics, offshore freight, radiopharmaceutical delivery trials and test cargo.

summaryBlocks.heading: No Federal Money
summaryBlocks.body: The FAA's eIPP page says participants bear their own costs. Louisiana's announcement states no funding, Florida's selection came with no allocated federal money, and no dollar amount for Texas's Project Nexus appears in any TxDOT or FAA source. The program does not change the type certification clock for passenger aircraft.

updateHistory.description: Lead, not applied to a card (corrected by the LAE editor on October 23, 2026: Aviation Week's report of October 23 covers the Albuquerque flights the FAA announced on October 19, and the monitor had dated them by the report): Reliable Robotics announced the launch of its eIPP project in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

Project cards rebuilt from the LAE Ecosystem Survey's primary sources (FAA eIPP page and map of October 16, 2026, FAA, state and company releases). Earlier automatic entries had filed company and stock news under the wrong projects. They are removed here and kept in this repository's history.

projects.sponsor: Port Authority of New York & New Jersey
projects.region: New York, New Jersey, Delaware and Vermont on the FAA map · 12 operational concepts
projects.keyOp: 12 operational concepts, including eVTOL passenger operations at the Manhattan heliport (FAA, March 9, 2026)
projects.milestone: No eIPP flight announced through October 22, 2026. Joby flew JFK to three Manhattan heliports for nine days in April 2026, with no passengers, and called it a celebration of the selection.
projects.opsTarget: Each participant committed to an eIPP flight within 90 days of signing its agreement (FAA)
projects.notes: The lead is the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, a bi-state authority, not a state transportation department. The FAA's March 9, 2026, announcement placed the project 'across New England' and named Archer, BETA, Electra and Joby. The FAA's eIPP map of October 16, 2026, gives the area as New York, New Jersey, Delaware and Vermont and lists BETA, Electra and Joby, without Archer. The Port Authority's own release of April 1, 2026, adds Wisk, the New York City Economic Development Corporation and NJEDA as proposal partners and names JFK, LaGuardia and Newark Liberty. No FAA release through October 22, 2026, announces a flight under this project.

projects.region: Texas Triangle · FAA map: Texas, Louisiana, Oklahoma
projects.keyOp: Project Nexus: phased testing from conventional aircraft to medical and cargo logistics to passenger air taxi flights across the Texas Triangle
projects.milestone: Project Nexus phase one launched at Fort Worth Alliance Airport on September 10, 2026, with helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft and no passengers (TxDOT).
projects.opsTarget: Passenger air taxi flights in the final phase, over the next three years (TxDOT)
projects.notes: TxDOT calls the project Project Nexus. Phase one, launched September 10, 2026, flies traditional aircraft such as helicopters and fixed-wing planes with no passengers. Later phases test medical and cargo logistics between rural facilities and medical centers in Austin and San Antonio, and the final phase carries passengers. Joby flew its own eVTOL demonstration campaign from its Fort Worth base the same week, and BETA says its first Texas flight under the program was an ALIA CTOL demonstration with Metro Aviation and Washington County EMS in Brenham in September 2026. No dollar amount appears in any TxDOT or FAA source. Wisk is subject to Archer's pending acquisition of Boeing's Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid subsidiaries, announced August 10, 2026.

projects.region: uFLY: Utah, Arizona, Idaho, Oklahoma and Oregon
projects.focus: Cargo, Medical, Emergency Response, Wildfire, then Passenger
projects.keyOp: Three years of cargo, emergency response, wildfire and eventual passenger testing across five states (UDOT)
projects.milestone: BETA concluded five days of uFLY operations with its all-electric ALIA CTOL and Alpine Air Express on October 7, 2026, testing radiopharmaceutical delivery.
projects.notes: UDOT leads uFLY: America's AAM Crossroads to the West, with Oregon, Idaho, Arizona and Oklahoma. Three flight campaigns identified by October 22, 2026, all airplanes from runways: Ampaire's hybrid-electric Cessna Skymaster conversion from Salt Lake City to Cedar City on August 6, Joby's remotely operated Cessna Caravan (J208) on September 30 (UDOT), and BETA's ALIA CTOL with Alpine Air Express, five days ending October 7. Joby also held uFLY demonstrations in Oklahoma City on September 29 and Portland on October 2. The FAA map of October 16, 2026, also lists Archer and Electra as partners, which no UDOT document names. Participants bear their own costs (FAA).

projects.region: NASAO AAM Multistate Collaborative · 17 states on the FAA map
projects.keyOp: Regional flights across many states, including routes similar to those of the Essential Air Service program (FAA)
projects.milestone: Electra announced EL2 instrument procedure flights from heliports and vertiports in Virginia on September 22, 2026. The program's first operational flights were BETA's, July 10, 2026.
projects.notes: PennDOT leads the NASAO AAM Multistate Collaborative. The FAA said on March 9, 2026, that it would work across 13 states. Its eIPP map of October 16, 2026, lists 17, and Pivotal's release of May 26, 2026, names 18 with Delaware, which the FAA map places in the Port Authority project. PennDOT and the FAA completed the program's first OTA on July 9, 2026 (FAA timeline). On July 10, 2026, BETA flew its conventional-takeoff ALIA from Virginia to Frederick and Martin State in Maryland carrying an organ for United Therapeutics, the program's first operational flights, all outside Pennsylvania. The FAA announced Electra hybrid-electric demonstrations linking Manassas, New Jersey and Philadelphia on August 18, and Virginia announced a second demonstration with the EL2 on September 3. Team operators named by Pivotal: UPMC STAT MedEvac, Tri State Charter, United Therapeutics and Republic Airways.

projects.region: LIFTOff Louisiana · offshore energy · FAA map: Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Texas
projects.keyOp: Cargo and personnel flights over Gulf waters to energy industry locations, centered at Houma-Terrebonne Airport
projects.milestone: Elroy Air flew a week of autonomous, uncrewed Chaparral cargo flights from Houma-Terrebonne in late August 2026, the program's first remotely piloted flights (FAA, August 31).
projects.opsTarget: Operations expand only after safety benchmarks are met and approvals secured (DOTD)
projects.editorial: The Louisiana offshore energy project deserves close attention. Bristow Group, the operator partner, has been coordinating with the FAA on the Elroy Air Chaparral for over a year. When the helicopter industry's dominant offshore operator validates autonomous cargo as a viable replacement for manned supply runs, the cost calculus changes for every operator in the Gulf.
projects.notes: DOTD calls the project LIFTOff Louisiana. Its launch announcement of August 27, 2026, names BETA and Elroy Air as aircraft developers, Bristow Group and Metro Aviation as operators, and Fletcher Technical Community College and Nicholls State University as workforce and research partners, and states no funding. The Chaparral flights carried ordinary offshore freight: medical supplies, spare parts, food and water. The FAA map of October 16, 2026, lists MSU and Teros among partners. No executed agreement had been published as of October 19, 2026, and the state's Vertiport Development Fund, created in 2024, has never been appropriated money.

links.label: Elroy Air: first uncrewed eIPP flights

projects.focus: Multi-phase: Cargo, then Passenger, then Automation and Medical Response
projects.keyOp: Statewide effort in three phases of operations focused on cargo delivery, passenger transportation, automation and medical response (FAA)
projects.milestone: No eIPP flight announced in Florida as of October 12, 2026. FDOT's SunTrax campus at Auburndale had flown no eVTOL as of the LAE survey.
projects.opsTarget: SunTrax first three phases due December 2026, opening year 2027 (FDOT business plan)
projects.notes: FDOT owns the 775-acre SunTrax campus at Auburndale and is building vertiports on it. The FAA's March 9, 2026, fact sheet lists Archer, BETA, Electra and Joby. The FAA's eIPP blog, updated October 8, 2026, lists BETA, Electra, Joby and other companies for Florida and does not say Florida's operations have begun. The selection came with no federal money, and the state's vertiport funding law carries no appropriation. None of the named aircraft companies bases an aircraft in Florida.

projects.region: eLIFT-NC · North Carolina, with an autonomous corridor into Virginia
projects.keyOp: Piloted medical and regional operations, plus an autonomous flight operation extending into Virginia (FAA)
projects.milestone: FAA announced North Carolina's first demonstration flights on September 23, 2026: Joby and BETA flew, with conventional-takeoff aircraft in phase one.
projects.opsTarget: Hospital pad-to-pad eVTOL missions in phase three (NCDOT)
projects.notes: NCDOT's project is Electric Logistics and Integrated Flight Testing (eLIFT-NC). It is phased from training and baseline operations with electric conventional-takeoff aircraft, the Joby J208 and BETA CX300, through route and network development, to hospital pad-to-pad eVTOL missions in the third phase. NCDOT has held a lead seat in every FAA drone integration program: the 2017 to 2020 Integration Pilot Program, BEYOND and the eIPP. Selection is not itself an operating authorization.

projects.region: City of Albuquerque · FAA map: New Mexico and Colorado
projects.keyOp: Near-term autonomous and remotely piloted cargo operations across New Mexico and Colorado (FAA)
projects.milestone: Reliable Robotics flew a remotely piloted Cessna 208B Caravan in a two-day campaign at Albuquerque Sunport, with an onboard safety pilot (FAA, October 19, 2026).
projects.opsTarget: Daily cargo service to Santa Fe and Durango planned (Reliable)
projects.notes: The only city among the eight leads. Reliable says the automated Caravan performed auto-taxi, auto-takeoff and auto-landing in the Sunport's Class C airspace, supervised by a remote pilot at its Mountain View, California, headquarters more than 700 miles away, with a safety pilot on board. Neither release gives the flight dates. Reliable calls the Santa Fe and Durango cargo routes, flown by Reliable Airlines, planned. The FAA says participants bear their own costs and no federal funding is required.
